```{r recoverability-read, message=FALSE}
         length(setdiff(keys_m, keys_r)), " only in the table, ",
         length(setdiff(keys_r, keys_m)), " only in the ratings file).")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

wordcounts <- read_csv(
  PATH_WORDCOUNTS,
  col_types = cols(
    id          = col_character(),
    stimulus_id = col_character(),
    dimension   = col_character(),
    word        = col_character(),
    count       = col_integer()
  )
)
check_blind_columns(wordcounts, WORDCOUNT_COLS, "The word-count file")

vocabulary <- read_csv(
  PATH_VOCAB,
  col_types = cols(word = col_character(), n_responses = col_integer())
)
check_blind_columns(vocabulary, VOCABULARY_COLS, "The vocabulary file")

# Three consistency checks between the two files and the ratings.
# (a) Every word counted is in the vocabulary, with the same number of
#     responses behind it that the counts themselves show, and that number is
#     at least the notebook's floor.
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(wordcounts[, c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension",
                                        "word")]))
word_doc_freq <- wordcounts %>%
  count(word, name = "n_in_counts") %>%
  left_join(vocabulary, by = "word")
if (anyNA(word_doc_freq$n_responses)) {
  stop("The word-count file uses words the vocabulary file does not list.")
}
if (any(word_doc_freq$n_responses != word_doc_freq$n_in_counts)) {
  stop("The vocabulary file's n_responses disagrees with the word-count file.")
}
if (any(word_doc_freq$n_responses < NOTEBOOK_MIN_RESPONSES)) {
  stop("The word-count file keeps words that appear in fewer than ",
       NOTEBOOK_MIN_RESPONSES, " responses.")
}
# (b) Every response the counts name exists in the ratings file, so the join
#     of the rating and the arm below cannot manufacture rows.
stopifnot(all(wordcounts$dimension %in% DIM_LEVELS))
wordcounts <- wordcounts %>%
  mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = DIM_LEVELS))
unmatched <- wordcounts %>%
  distinct(id, stimulus_id, dimension) %>%
  anti_join(ratings, by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"))
if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
  stop("The word-count file names ", nrow(unmatched),
       " response(s) the ratings file does not have.")
}
# (c) The size of the corpus the models will see, printed so that a reader
#     can judge the counts against it. A response that used no counted word
#     has no row here and enters the matrices below as a row of zeros.
n_resp_with_word <- nrow(distinct(wordcounts, id, stimulus_id, dimension))
cat("Word-count file: ", nrow(wordcounts), " response-word rows, ",
    n_distinct(wordcounts$word), " words (each in at least ",
    NOTEBOOK_MIN_RESPONSES, " responses), covering ", n_resp_with_word,
    " of ", nrow(ratings), " responses; the remaining ",
    nrow(ratings) - n_resp_with_word,
    " used no counted word and enter the models as a row of zeros.\n",
    sep = "")
```

```{r recoverability-helpers}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HOW THE CHECK IS MEASURED.
#
# The question is: given only the words a person wrote, how well can the
# number they gave be guessed, and how well can the arm they were in be
# guessed? Each is answered by fitting a model on some responses and scoring
# it on responses it has never seen, because a model scored on the responses
# it was fitted to can look good by memorising them.
#
# The model is ridge regression: an ordinary regression of the outcome on
# every kept word's count at once, with a penalty added that pulls every
# coefficient toward zero. With several hundred words and about a thousand
# responses an unpenalised regression would fit noise, and the penalty is
# what makes the fit usable. How hard to pull is set by a tuning constant,
# lambda, and lambda is chosen by inner cross-validation: within the training
# responses the model is fitted on nine tenths and scored on the tenth left
# out, for each of ten such splits and for each value of lambda on a fixed
# grid, and the lambda with the best average score is kept. The grid is fixed
# rather than derived from each training set so that every fold, every
# permutation and every study searches the same candidates. For the arm the
# same machinery is run as a logistic regression (section 3.1.1 explains the
# term), so the model predicts a probability of being in the AI arm.
#
# The outer split is ten folds GROUPED BY PARTICIPANT: all of a participant's
# responses fall in one fold, so no participant is ever on both the training
# and the test side. That matters because people repeat themselves; a model
# that had seen eight of a person's explanations could guess the ninth from
# their habits alone, which would recover the person and not the rating. The
# inner splits are grouped the same way. The predictions collected from the
# ten test folds are "out-of-fold" predictions: every response is predicted
# by a model that never saw it or its author, and every statistic below is
# computed on those.
#
# THE VOCABULARY IS BUILT INSIDE EACH TRAINING FOLD. The registered floor
# keeps a word only if it appears in at least five responses, so that a word
# almost nobody used carries little weight. Counted over the whole corpus,
# that floor lets the held-out participants decide which words become
# columns, which is not label leakage (no rating or arm is involved) but is
# still information from the people the model is supposed never to have seen.
# So the floor is applied, for each outer fold, to the training responses of
# the dimension being modelled, and the held-out responses are scored on
# those columns only. The inner cross-validation uses the outer fold's
# vocabulary. Five responses can come from fewer than five people, so the
# floor is a guard against rare words and not a guarantee that no word is
# one person's habit; the grouped folds are what keep a habit from scoring.
#
# For the rating the statistic is the Pearson correlation r between the
# out-of-fold prediction and the observed rating: how far the two move
# together, from zero (not at all) to one (perfectly). A model that has
# shrunk every coefficient to nothing predicts the same number for every
# response, and a constant has no correlation with anything; that case is
# scored as zero, which is what it is: no recovery. For the arm the statistic
# is the AUC, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve,
# read here as the probability that a randomly chosen AI-arm response is given
# a higher predicted probability of being AI-arm than a randomly chosen
# human-arm response. One half is coin-flipping; one is perfect separation.
# It is computed by hand from the rank formula (the Mann-Whitney identity:
# rank every response by its score, sum the AI-arm ranks, subtract the
# smallest sum they could have had, divide by the number of AI-human pairs),
# so no further package is needed.
#
# TWO KINDS OF UNCERTAINTY are reported beside each statistic. The 95 percent
# interval comes from resampling participants 2,000 times over the
# out-of-fold predictions, with boot_by_participant() from section 2.5; it
# says how much the statistic would move under a fresh sample of people,
# holding the fitted models fixed, so it leaves out the variation that
# refitting the models on that fresh sample would add. The permutation null
# says what the statistic looks like when the link it is about has been cut:
# the outcome is shuffled, the whole pipeline is run again on the shuffled
# outcome, and the 95th percentile of the shuffled statistics is the bar a
# real one has to clear.
#
# WHAT EACH SHUFFLE CUTS. For the rating the shuffle is RESTRICTED: each
# participant's ten ratings in the dimension are shuffled among that same
# participant's ten explanations, so every person keeps their own ratings and
# their own average, and only which image got which rating is scrambled. The
# null therefore keeps whatever the words can recover about a person's
# general level, and an observed r above it says the words carry which images
# a person rated higher. That is the target, stated in words: whether the
# words predict, within a person, which images got the higher ratings. An
# unrestricted shuffle across all responses would break the
# participant and image structure the real ratings have, and would set too
# low a bar for that target. For the arm the shuffle is across
# PARTICIPANTS: each participant keeps one label and the labels are dealt out
# afresh among them, so the shuffled arm keeps the structure the real one
# has, one arm per person, and a model cannot clear the bar merely by
# learning who wrote what.
#
# Beside the arm-from-words AUC sit two models of the arm that use the
# RATING: an ordinary logistic regression of the arm on the rating alone, and
# a ridge logistic regression on the rating and the word counts together,
# with the rating left unpenalised so that it enters as it does in the
# rating-only model and only the words are shrunk. Both are scored on the
# same ten folds and the same held-out participants, and the difference
# between their AUCs, with an interval from resampling participants over the
# paired held-out predictions, is the incremental AUC: how much the words add
# to the rating in telling the arms apart. The stand-alone AUCs of the words
# and of the rating are descriptive references, and the gap between them is
# not that quantity, since two predictors can score alike alone and still
# carry different information.
#
# RUNTIME AND REPRODUCIBILITY. One pass of the pipeline (ten outer fits, each
# with its inner cross-validation) takes a few seconds, and each dimension
# needs one pass for each observed model and N_PERM shuffled passes for the
# rating and for the arm, so the shuffled passes are run on several cores at
# once with parallel::mclapply() where the platform allows it (not on
# Windows, where they run in sequence). Every random draw, the fold
# assignments and the shuffled outcomes alike, is made before the parallel
# section starts, so the numbers do not depend on how many cores were used,
# and the seed is the file's seed constant. If a machine has to run the
# passes in sequence and that exceeds the ten-minute target, set N_PERM to
# 100L; the table records whichever number was used.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

N_OUTER_FOLDS <- 10L
N_PERM        <- 200L
RECOVER_SEED  <- 20260421L
LAMBDA_GRID   <- exp(seq(log(1e4), log(1e-3), length.out = 100))
N_WORKERS     <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1L else
                   max(1L, min(8L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))

# Deal participants into K folds, balanced across the two arms so that every
# fold holds responses from both. Returns fold numbers named by participant.
participant_folds <- function(id_arm, K) {
  fold <- integer(nrow(id_arm))
  for (arm in TYPE_LEVELS) {
    rows <- which(id_arm$Type == arm)
    fold[rows] <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(K), length(rows)))
  }
  setNames(fold, id_arm$id)
}

# One dimension's responses in a fixed order, its word counts, and its
# participants with their arms. Sections 8.1 and 9.3 both start here, so the
# two see the same rows in the same order.
dimension_frame <- function(dim_name) {
  resp <- ratings %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    arrange(id, stimulus_id)
  counts <- wordcounts %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name) %>%
    semi_join(resp, by = c("id", "stimulus_id"))
  id_arm <- resp %>% distinct(id, Type) %>% arrange(id)
  list(resp = resp, counts = counts, id_arm = id_arm)
}

# The words that appear in at least WORD_MIN_RESPONSES of the responses
# marked TRUE in `rows`, which index `resp`. This is the registered floor,
# applied to whichever responses a model is allowed to learn from.
floor_vocabulary <- function(resp, counts, rows) {
  keys <- paste(resp$id, resp$stimulus_id)[rows]
  counts %>%
    filter(paste(id, stimulus_id) %in% keys) %>%
    count(word, name = "n_responses") %>%
    filter(n_responses >= WORD_MIN_RESPONSES) %>%
    arrange(word)
}

# The response-by-word matrix for one dimension. Rows follow `resp`, that
# dimension's responses in a fixed order; columns are `words`; cells are
# counts, mostly zero, so the matrix is stored sparsely (only the non-zero
# cells are kept in memory), which is the form glmnet takes directly.
response_word_matrix <- function(resp, counts, words) {
  key_resp <- paste(resp$id, resp$stimulus_id)
  cnt <- counts %>% filter(word %in% words)
  Matrix::sparseMatrix(
    i = match(paste(cnt$id, cnt$stimulus_id), key_resp),
    j = match(cnt$word, words),
    x = as.numeric(cnt$count),
    dims = c(nrow(resp), length(words)),
    dimnames = list(NULL, words)
  )
}

# Out-of-fold ridge predictions on the response scale (the rating itself for
# the gaussian model, a probability for the binomial one). `X_list[[k]]` is
# the matrix on fold k's training vocabulary; `outer_fold` gives each
# response's fold; `inner_folds[[k]]` gives the inner fold of each training
# response when fold k is held out. `unpenalised`, when given, is a column
# added to every fold's matrix with a penalty factor of zero, so that glmnet
# fits its coefficient without shrinking it.
ridge_oof <- function(X_list, y, family, outer_fold, inner_folds,
                      unpenalised = NULL) {
  pred <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
  for (k in seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {
    tr <- outer_fold != k
    X  <- X_list[[k]]
    pf <- rep(1, ncol(X))
    if (!is.null(unpenalised)) {
      X  <- cbind(Matrix::Matrix(unpenalised, ncol = 1, sparse = TRUE,
                                 dimnames = list(NULL, "rating")), X)
      pf <- c(0, pf)
    }
    cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
      X[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr],
      family = family, alpha = 0, lambda = LAMBDA_GRID,
      foldid = inner_folds[[k]], penalty.factor = pf
    )
    pred[!tr] <- as.numeric(predict(cv, X[!tr, , drop = FALSE],
                                    s = "lambda.min", type = "response"))
  }
  pred
}

# The comparison model: the arm from the rating alone, same outer folds.
rating_oof <- function(rating, y, outer_fold) {
  d    <- data.frame(y = y, rating = rating)
  pred <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
  for (k in seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {
    tr  <- outer_fold != k
    fit <- glm(y ~ rating, data = d[tr, , drop = FALSE], family = binomial)
    pred[!tr] <- unname(predict(fit, newdata = d[!tr, , drop = FALSE],
                                type = "response"))
  }
  pred
}

# Pearson r with a constant prediction scored as zero (see the comment
# above), and the AUC by the rank formula, with ties given their average
# rank as the Mann-Whitney identity requires.
oof_r <- function(pred, obs) {
  if (sd(pred) < 1e-12 || sd(obs) < 1e-12) return(0)
  cor(pred, obs)
}

auc_rank <- function(score, is_positive) {
  n1 <- sum(is_positive)
  n0 <- sum(!is_positive)
  if (n1 == 0 || n0 == 0) return(NA_real_)
  r <- rank(score)
  (sum(r[is_positive]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}

# Run one function over a list of pre-drawn shuffled outcomes, in parallel
# where the platform allows it. Nothing inside draws a random number, so the
# result is the same whatever N_WORKERS is. A failure in a worker is raised
# here rather than returned as a silent gap in the null.
run_permutations <- function(items, f) {
  out <- if (N_WORKERS > 1L) {
    parallel::mclapply(items, f, mc.cores = N_WORKERS, mc.set.seed = FALSE)
  } else {
    lapply(items, f)
  }
  failed <- vapply(out, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
  if (any(failed)) {
    stop("A permuted pass failed: ", conditionMessage(attr(out[[which(failed)[1]]], "condition")))
  }
  unlist(out)
}

# Evaluate an expression and keep every warning it raised. glmnet reports a
# path that stopped short of convergence as a warning, and so does glm for a
# separation problem; any warning from an observed fit gives that dimension's
# rows the status nonconvergence, and the warnings themselves go in the note.
with_warnings <- function(expr) {
  warns <- character()
  value <- withCallingHandlers(
    expr,
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
  list(value = value, warnings = unique(warns))
}

# The whole check for one rating dimension: the matrices, the folds, the
# observed statistics, their intervals, and the three permutation nulls.
recoverability_for_dimension <- function(dim_name) {

  fr     <- dimension_frame(dim_name)
  resp   <- fr$resp
  counts <- fr$counts
  id_arm <- fr$id_arm

  # Every random draw happens here, in a fixed order from the seed: the outer
  # folds, the inner folds for each outer fold, then the shuffled outcomes.
  set.seed(RECOVER_SEED)
  outer_by_id <- participant_folds(id_arm, N_OUTER_FOLDS)
  outer_fold  <- unname(outer_by_id[resp$id])
  inner_folds <- lapply(seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS), function(k) {
    tr          <- outer_fold != k
    inner_by_id <- participant_folds(id_arm %>% filter(id %in% resp$id[tr]),
                                     N_OUTER_FOLDS)
    unname(inner_by_id[resp$id[tr]])
  })
  y_rating <- resp$rating
  y_arm    <- as.integer(resp$Type == "AI")
  # The restricted rating shuffle: within each participant, that person's
  # ratings are reassigned among their own explanations.
  perm_rating <- replicate(N_PERM, {
    ave(y_rating, resp$id, FUN = function(v) v[sample.int(length(v))])
  }, simplify = FALSE)
  perm_arm <- replicate(N_PERM, {
    dealt <- setNames(sample(as.character(id_arm$Type)), id_arm$id)
    as.integer(dealt[resp$id] == "AI")
  }, simplify = FALSE)

  # One matrix per outer fold, on that fold's training vocabulary. These
  # depend on no outcome, so the shuffled passes reuse them.
  vocab_by_fold <- lapply(seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS), function(k) {
    floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, outer_fold != k)$word
  })
  X_list <- lapply(vocab_by_fold, function(w) {
    response_word_matrix(resp, counts, w)
  })
  n_feat <- vapply(X_list, ncol, integer(1))

  # The observed out-of-fold predictions, with any warning they raised.
  observed <- with_warnings(list(
    pred_rating = ridge_oof(X_list, y_rating, "gaussian", outer_fold,
                            inner_folds),
    pred_arm    = ridge_oof(X_list, y_arm, "binomial", outer_fold,
                            inner_folds),
    pred_arm_from_rating = rating_oof(y_rating, y_arm, outer_fold),
    pred_arm_rating_words = ridge_oof(X_list, y_arm, "binomial", outer_fold,
                                      inner_folds, unpenalised = y_rating)
  ))
  status <- if (length(observed$warnings) == 0) "ok" else "nonconvergence"
  note   <- if (length(observed$warnings) == 0) {
    "status ok; no warning from any observed fit"
  } else {
    paste0("status nonconvergence; ", paste(observed$warnings, collapse = "; "))
  }
  pr <- observed$value

  # The permutation nulls, same pipeline on the shuffled outcomes.
  null_r <- run_permutations(perm_rating, function(yp) {
    oof_r(ridge_oof(X_list, yp, "gaussian", outer_fold, inner_folds), yp)
  })
  null_auc_words <- run_permutations(perm_arm, function(yp) {
    auc_rank(ridge_oof(X_list, yp, "binomial", outer_fold, inner_folds),
             yp == 1L)
  })
  null_auc_rating <- vapply(perm_arm, function(yp) {
    suppressWarnings(auc_rank(rating_oof(y_rating, yp, outer_fold), yp == 1L))
  }, numeric(1))

  # Participant-resampled intervals over the out-of-fold predictions. The
  # incremental AUC is computed inside each replicate from the paired
  # predictions of the same drawn participants.
  oof <- tibble(
    id                    = resp$id,
    obs_rating            = y_rating,
    obs_arm               = y_arm == 1L,
    pred_rating           = pr$pred_rating,
    pred_arm              = pr$pred_arm,
    pred_arm_from_rating  = pr$pred_arm_from_rating,
    pred_arm_rating_words = pr$pred_arm_rating_words
  )
  boot <- boot_by_participant(oof, function(d) {
    auc_r  <- auc_rank(d$pred_arm_from_rating, d$obs_arm)
    auc_rw <- auc_rank(d$pred_arm_rating_words, d$obs_arm)
    c(rating_from_words          = oof_r(d$pred_rating, d$obs_rating),
      arm_from_words             = auc_rank(d$pred_arm, d$obs_arm),
      arm_from_rating            = auc_r,
      arm_from_rating_plus_words = auc_rw,
      incremental_auc            = auc_rw - auc_r)
  }, seed = RECOVER_SEED)

  eligible <- status %in% ELIGIBLE_STATUS
  fold_vocab_text <- paste0("words in at least ", WORD_MIN_RESPONSES,
                            " training explanations of this dimension, ",
                            "rebuilt in each outer fold")
  tibble(
    dimension  = dim_name,
    target     = c("rating", "arm", "arm", "arm", "arm"),
    predictors = c("words", "words", "rating", "rating plus words",
                   "incremental AUC (rating plus words minus rating)"),
    statistic  = c("out-of-fold Pearson r, predicted vs observed rating",
                   "out-of-fold AUC, AI arm as the positive class",
                   "out-of-fold AUC, AI arm as the positive class",
                   "out-of-fold AUC, AI arm as the positive class",
                   paste0("difference in out-of-fold AUC, rating plus words ",
                          "minus rating, same held-out participants")),
    estimate   = boot$estimate,
    ci_low     = if (eligible) boot$ci_lo else NA_real_,
    ci_high    = if (eligible) boot$ci_hi else NA_real_,
    null_95th  = if (eligible) c(quantile(null_r,          0.95, names = FALSE),
                                 quantile(null_auc_words,  0.95, names = FALSE),
                                 quantile(null_auc_rating, 0.95, names = FALSE),
                                 NA_real_, NA_real_)
                 else NA_real_,
    n_perm     = c(N_PERM, N_PERM, N_PERM, NA_integer_, NA_integer_),
    n_folds    = N_OUTER_FOLDS,
    n_features = c(median(n_feat), median(n_feat), 1, median(n_feat) + 1,
                   NA_real_),
    n_features_min = c(min(n_feat), min(n_feat), 1, min(n_feat) + 1, NA_real_),
    n_features_max = c(max(n_feat), max(n_feat), 1, max(n_feat) + 1, NA_real_),
    seed       = RECOVER_SEED,
    n_boot     = boot$B,
    n_valid    = boot$n_valid,
    n_responses    = nrow(resp),
    n_participants = nrow(id_arm),
    n_responses_without_kept_word = sum(Matrix::rowSums(X_list[[1]]) == 0),
    vocabulary = c(fold_vocab_text, fold_vocab_text, "none",
                   fold_vocab_text, fold_vocab_text),
    model = c(paste0("ridge regression (glmnet, alpha = 0), lambda by inner ",
                     "ten-fold cross-validation grouped by participant"),
              paste0("ridge logistic regression (glmnet, alpha = 0), lambda ",
                     "by inner ten-fold cross-validation grouped by participant"),
              "logistic regression, arm ~ rating, same outer folds",
              paste0("ridge logistic regression on the rating and the word ",
                     "counts, rating unpenalised (penalty factor 0), lambda by ",
                     "inner ten-fold cross-validation grouped by participant"),
              paste0("paired difference of the two rows above, scored on the ",
                     "same held-out participants")),
    permutation = c(paste0("rating shuffled among each participant's own ",
                           "explanations in this dimension; keeps each ",
                           "person's level, so an r above it means the words ",
                           "carry which images a person rated higher"),
                    "arm shuffled across participants",
                    "arm shuffled across participants",
                    "none", "none"),
    status = status,
    note   = note
  )
}
```

```{r recoverability-run}
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_recoverability.csv"))

recoverability <- run_or_report(
  "8.1 how closely the words track the rating and the arm, both dimensions",
  function() bind_rows(lapply(DIM_LEVELS, recoverability_for_dimension))
)

if (!is.null(recoverability)) {
  recoverability %>%
    select(dimension, target, predictors, estimate, ci_low, ci_high,
           null_95th, n_perm, n_features, status) %>%
    print(width = Inf)
  write_csv(recoverability,
            file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_recoverability.csv"))

  # The reading, in words, one block per dimension. The registered rule for
  # the stand-alone scores has two clauses: recovery is read as present when
  # the estimate lies above the null's 95th percentile AND the interval is
  # clear of the chance value, 0 for r and 0.5 for the AUC. When either
  # clause fails the check has not shown recovery, which is a different thing
  # from showing there is none, and the branches below say which clause
  # failed. The incremental AUC has no null; its interval is read against
  # zero, and an interval that includes zero is inconclusive.
  for (dim_name in DIM_LEVELS) {
    r  <- recoverability %>% filter(dimension == dim_name)
    rw <- r %>% filter(target == "rating")
    aw <- r %>% filter(target == "arm", predictors == "words")
    ar <- r %>% filter(target == "arm", predictors == "rating")
    ab <- r %>% filter(target == "arm", predictors == "rating plus words")
    ai <- r %>% filter(target == "arm", grepl("^incremental", predictors))

    cat("\n", dim_name, " explanations (", rw$n_responses, " responses from ",
        rw$n_participants, " participants, ", rw$n_features_min, " to ",
        rw$n_features_max, " words per training fold):\n", sep = "")

    if (rw$status != "ok") {
      cat("  No reading: the observed fits have status ", rw$status,
          "; see the note column.\n", sep = "")
      next
    }

    cat("  Rating from words: out-of-fold r = ", fmt_num(rw$estimate),
        " (95% interval ", fmt_num(rw$ci_low), " to ", fmt_num(rw$ci_high),
        "); with each participant's ratings shuffled among their own ",
        "explanations, r reaches ", fmt_num(rw$null_95th),
        " at the 95th percentile over ", rw$n_perm, " permutations.\n",
        sep = "")
    if (rw$estimate > rw$null_95th && rw$ci_low > 0) {
      cat("    The words track the rating more closely than they do when ",
          "each person's ratings are shuffled among that person's own ",
          "explanations, and the interval is clear of zero, so the ",
          "registered rule reads recovery as present: the words carry which ",
          "of a person's images got the higher ratings, beyond that person's ",
          "overall level. Words written after the rating can track it this ",
          "way without having produced it, which is one reason sections 3 ",
          "and 4 read their associations as denotation and not as ",
          "mechanism.\n", sep = "")
    } else if (rw$estimate <= rw$null_95th) {
      cat("    The words do not track the rating beyond what the ",
          "within-person shuffle produces, so this check does not show that ",
          "they carry which images a person rated higher. That is not ",
          "evidence that they carry nothing about the rating.\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("    The estimate lies above the shuffled ratings' 95th percentile, ",
          "but its interval reaches zero, so the registered rule does not ",
          "read recovery as present. That is not evidence that the words ",
          "carry nothing about the rating.\n", sep = "")
    }

    cat("  Arm from words: out-of-fold AUC = ", fmt_num(aw$estimate),
        " (95% interval ", fmt_num(aw$ci_low), " to ", fmt_num(aw$ci_high),
        "); arms shuffled across participants reach AUC = ",
        fmt_num(aw$null_95th), " at their 95th percentile.\n", sep = "")
    if (aw$estimate <= aw$null_95th) {
      cat("    The words do not tell the arms apart beyond what shuffled ",
          "arms produce, so this check does not show that they carry the ",
          "arm.\n", sep = "")
    } else if (aw$ci_low <= 0.5) {
      cat("    The AUC lies above the shuffled arms' 95th percentile, but its ",
          "interval reaches the chance value of 0.5, so the registered rule ",
          "does not read recovery as present.\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("    The words tell the arms apart better than shuffled arms do, ",
          "with an interval clear of 0.5.\n", sep = "")
    }

    cat("  Arm from the rating alone: AUC = ", fmt_num(ar$estimate),
        " (95% interval ", fmt_num(ar$ci_low), " to ", fmt_num(ar$ci_high),
        "). Arm from the rating and the words together: AUC = ",
        fmt_num(ab$estimate), " (95% interval ", fmt_num(ab$ci_low), " to ",
        fmt_num(ab$ci_high), ").\n",
        "  Incremental AUC, rating plus words minus rating, on the same ",
        "held-out participants: ", fmt_num(ai$estimate), " (95% interval ",
        fmt_num(ai$ci_low), " to ", fmt_num(ai$ci_high), ").\n", sep = "")
    if (ai$ci_low > 0) {
      cat("    On these held-out participants the words carry information ",
          "about the arm beyond what the rating carries.\n", sep = "")
    } else if (ai$ci_high < 0) {
      cat("    Adding the words lowers the held-out AUC: on these ",
          "participants the penalised model of the rating and the words ",
          "tells the arms apart less well than the rating alone.\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("    The interval includes zero, so this check does not show that ",
          "the words add to the rating in telling the arms apart; that is ",
          "not evidence that they add nothing.\n", sep = "")
    }
  }
  cat("\nAll of these are descriptive. They enter no correction family and ",
      "support no prediction. Each interval holds the fitted models fixed ",
      "and resamples participants over their held-out predictions.\n",
      sep = "")
}

# WHAT TO LOOK AT: the rating-from-words r against its within-person null,
# which says whether the words carry which images a person rated higher, and
# the incremental AUC, which says whether the words add anything to the
# rating in telling the two arms apart.
```

## 8.2 Within-person word overlap by arm

```{r selfsimilarity-read, message=FALSE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE TOKEN TABLE, AND WHAT IS COMPUTED FROM IT.
#
# nlp/study1_text_tokens.csv has one row per response: id, stimulus_id,
# dimension, and content_words, the response's distinct content words in
# lower case, sorted and joined by single spaces (empty when the response has
# none). It carries no arm and no rating. From it this chunk computes, for
# each participant and rating dimension:
#
#   self_overlap     the mean Jaccard overlap across the 45 pairs of the
#                    participant's ten explanations. The Jaccard overlap of
#                    two word sets is the number of words in both divided by
#                    the number of words in either, so it runs from zero (no
#                    word shared) to one (the same words).
#   stranger_overlap the same overlap between each of the ten explanations and
#                    the explanations OTHER participants wrote for the same
#                    image and the same dimension, averaged first over those
#                    other participants and then over the ten images. Two
#                    people who saw the same picture share words because the
#                    picture supplies them (a cat, a sunset), and this is how
#                    much of that sharing to expect.
#   self_minus_stranger  the difference: how much more a person's explanations
#                    resemble each other than they resemble strangers'
#                    explanations of the same pictures. This is the reuse that
#                    belongs to the person rather than to the image, and it is
#                    the quantity the arms are compared on.
#   mean_words       the average number of distinct content words per
#                    explanation, carried because the overlap statistic
#                    depends on how much a person writes.
#   n_texts          how many explanations had any content word. An
#                    explanation with none drops out of both overlaps.
#
# The overlaps are computed here rather than in the notebook because the
# stranger baseline depends on WHO the other participants are. A bootstrap
# replicate draws a new set of participants, and the baseline for each of
# them has to be rebuilt from the others drawn into that replicate; a table
# of baselines fixed in advance would hold the reference group constant and
# understate the uncertainty. So the Jaccard overlap between every pair of
# participants' explanations of each image is computed once, as a matrix per
# image and dimension, and each replicate reweights it by how many times each
# participant was drawn. On the full sample, with every weight equal to one,
# these are the overlaps the registered definition gives.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
tokens <- read_csv(
  PATH_TOKENS,
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character()
)
check_blind_columns(tokens, TOKENS_COLS, "The token file")
check_response_keys(tokens, "The token file")
stopifnot(all(tokens$dimension %in% DIM_LEVELS))

participant_ids <- sort(unique(ratings$id))
image_ids       <- sort(unique(ratings$stimulus_id))

# One list of word sets per dimension: word_sets[[dim]][[image]][[id]].
split_words <- function(s) if (nzchar(s)) strsplit(s, " ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]] else character(0)

jaccard <- function(a, b) {
  u <- length(union(a, b))
  if (u == 0) NA_real_ else length(intersect(a, b)) / u
}

# For one dimension: the stranger matrices (overlap of participant i's
# explanation of an image with participant j's, zero on the diagonal and in
# the column of an empty explanation), the matching indicator of which
# entries count, and each participant's self overlap, mean_words and n_texts.
overlap_inputs <- function(dim_name) {
  tk <- tokens %>% filter(dimension == dim_name)
  sets <- lapply(image_ids, function(s) {
    t_s <- tk %>% filter(stimulus_id == s)
    w   <- lapply(t_s$content_words, split_words)
    names(w) <- t_s$id
    w[participant_ids]
  })
  names(sets) <- image_ids
  n <- length(participant_ids)

  J <- V <- vector("list", length(image_ids))
  names(J) <- names(V) <- image_ids
  for (s in image_ids) {
    w   <- sets[[s]]
    ok  <- vapply(w, length, integer(1)) > 0
    m   <- matrix(0, n, n)
    for (i in which(ok)) for (j in which(ok)) {
      if (i < j) m[i, j] <- m[j, i] <- jaccard(w[[i]], w[[j]])
    }
    v <- matrix(rep(as.numeric(ok), each = n), n, n)
    diag(v) <- 0
    J[[s]] <- m
    V[[s]] <- v
  }

  per_person <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    own <- Filter(length, lapply(image_ids, function(s) sets[[s]][[i]]))
    pairs <- if (length(own) >= 2) {
      combn(length(own), 2, function(p) jaccard(own[[p[1]]], own[[p[2]]]))
    } else numeric(0)
    tibble(id = participant_ids[i], n_texts = length(own),
           self_overlap = if (length(pairs)) mean(pairs) else NA_real_,
           mean_words = if (length(own)) mean(lengths(own)) else NA_real_)
  })
  has_text <- sapply(image_ids, function(s) lengths(sets[[s]]) > 0)
  list(J = J, V = V, person = bind_rows(per_person), has_text = has_text)
}

# The stranger overlap of every participant, given how many times each
# participant was drawn (w, one weight per participant_ids entry). A
# participant drawn twice counts twice among everyone else's strangers and
# never as their own stranger.
stranger_overlap_given <- function(inp, w) {
  per_image <- sapply(names(inp$J), function(s) {
    num <- as.numeric(inp$J[[s]] %*% w)
    den <- as.numeric(inp$V[[s]] %*% w)
    ifelse(inp$has_text[, s] & den > 0, num / den, NA_real_)
  })
  rowMeans(per_image, na.rm = TRUE) * ifelse(rowSums(!is.na(per_image)) > 0, 1, NA)
}

overlap_by_dim <- lapply(DIM_LEVELS, overlap_inputs)
names(overlap_by_dim) <- DIM_LEVELS

id_type <- ratings %>% distinct(id, Type) %>%
  mutate(id = as.character(id)) %>%
  arrange(id)
stopifnot(identical(id_type$id, participant_ids))

selfsim <- bind_rows(lapply(DIM_LEVELS, function(dim_name) {
  inp <- overlap_by_dim[[dim_name]]
  inp$person %>%
    mutate(dimension = factor(dim_name, levels = DIM_LEVELS),
           stranger_overlap = stranger_overlap_given(inp, rep(1, length(participant_ids))),
           self_minus_stranger = self_overlap - stranger_overlap) %>%
    left_join(id_type, by = "id")
}))
stopifnot(nrow(distinct(selfsim, id, dimension)) == nrow(selfsim))

# A participant with fewer than two explanations in a dimension has no pairs
# to overlap and no self_overlap; such rows are counted and left out of the
# comparison, though their explanations still serve as strangers to others.
n_no_pairs <- sum(is.na(selfsim$self_minus_stranger))
cat("Overlaps computed for ", nrow(selfsim), " participant-by-dimension rows (",
    n_no_pairs, " without a pair of explanations to compare).\n", sep = "")
print(selfsim %>% filter(!is.na(self_minus_stranger)) %>%
        count(dimension, Type, name = "n_participants"))
```

```{r selfsimilarity-by-arm}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE COMPARISON. Within each dimension, self_minus_stranger is regressed on
# the arm with mean_words as a covariate, meaning a variable entered so that
# the arms are compared between participants who wrote the same amount:
#
#   self_minus_stranger ~ Type + mean_words
#
# an ordinary least-squares regression with one row per participant, so no
# random intercept is needed; the participant is the unit. The arm
# coefficient is the AI-minus-Human difference in own-word reuse at equal
# length, and it is the registered quantity. The length adjustment is not
# optional: the overlap statistic moves with how much a person writes, and
# the arms may differ in that, so an unadjusted difference could be a
# difference in verbosity wearing the wrong name.
#
# THE INTERVAL. 2,000 replicates, seed 20260421, each drawing participants
# with replacement WITHIN each arm, so the two arm sizes stay what the design
# delivered. In every replicate the stranger baseline is rebuilt from the
# participants drawn into it, a participant drawn twice counting twice among
# everyone else's strangers, and the model is refitted to the drawn rows. The
# interval is the middle 95 percent of the replicate coefficients, and it
# therefore carries the uncertainty of the reference group as well as that
# of the people compared.
#
# THE TEST AND ITS CORRECTION. This check carries a predicted direction (the
# machine arm reuses more, so the coefficient is predicted positive) and it
# is run on two dimensions, so the two are treated as one family of two
# tests and corrected together by the Holm procedure: the two p-values are
# ordered, the smaller is compared against .05 / 2, and only if it passes is
# the larger compared against .05; the Holm-adjusted p-values (p_holm)
# express the same thing as numbers to compare with .05. Each p-value comes
# from the replicates themselves: twice the share of replicate coefficients
# on the far side of zero, with one added to the count and to the number of
# replicates so that no p-value is reported as exactly zero, and capped at
# one. Up to that added one, it falls below a level alpha when the percentile
# interval at 1 minus alpha leaves zero out, so the smallest p-value 2,000
# replicates can give is about .001. The reading has three values:
#
#   supported           p_holm below .05 and the estimate positive, the
#                       predicted direction;
#   opposite direction  p_holm below .05 and the estimate negative, a
#                       reliable difference the other way;
#   inconclusive        p_holm at or above .05, which includes every 95
#                       percent interval that contains zero. Inconclusive is
#                       not evidence that the arms reuse their words equally.
#
# The reading comes from the Holm-adjusted p-value and the sign of the
# estimate, as the case_when() step below sets out. The uncorrected 95
# percent interval is reported beside it and does not decide the reading on
# its own. Three readings rather than a pass or a fail keep a null from being
# reported as a refutation.
#
# The raw self_overlap, stranger_overlap, self_minus_stranger and mean_words
# by arm are deposited beside the difference as description, with intervals
# from the same replicates, so a reader can see the levels the adjusted
# difference is made from.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"))

SELFSIM_SEED <- 20260421L

selfsim_arm_coef <- function(d) {
  d <- d[!is.na(d$self_minus_stranger), , drop = FALSE]
  fit <- tryCatch(lm(self_minus_stranger ~ Type + mean_words, data = d),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit) || !"TypeAI" %in% names(coef(fit))) return(NA_real_)
  unname(coef(fit)[["TypeAI"]])
}

selfsim_levels <- function(d) {
  out <- c()
  for (arm in TYPE_LEVELS) {
    dd <- d[d$Type == arm & !is.na(d$self_minus_stranger), , drop = FALSE]
    out[paste0("self_overlap_", arm)]        <- mean(dd$self_overlap)
    out[paste0("stranger_overlap_", arm)]    <- mean(dd$stranger_overlap)
    out[paste0("self_minus_stranger_", arm)] <- mean(dd$self_minus_stranger)
    out[paste0("mean_words_", arm)]          <- mean(dd$mean_words)
  }
  out
}

# One dimension: the observed coefficient and levels, then the replicates.
selfsim_dimension <- function(dim_name) {
  inp  <- overlap_by_dim[[dim_name]]
  base <- selfsim %>% filter(dimension == dim_name)
  stopifnot(identical(base$id, participant_ids))

  obs_fit <- tryCatch(lm(self_minus_stranger ~ Type + mean_words,
                         data = base %>% filter(!is.na(self_minus_stranger))),
                      error = function(e) e)
  status <- if (inherits(obs_fit, "error")) "error" else "ok"
  note   <- if (status == "ok") "status ok; ordinary least squares" else
    paste0("status error; ", conditionMessage(obs_fit))

  obs_coef   <- selfsim_arm_coef(base)
  obs_levels <- selfsim_levels(base)

  idx_by_arm <- split(seq_along(participant_ids), base$Type)
  set.seed(SELFSIM_SEED)
  reps <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = B_BOOT, ncol = 1 + length(obs_levels))
  for (b in seq_len(B_BOOT)) {
    drawn <- unlist(lapply(TYPE_LEVELS, function(arm) {
      ix <- idx_by_arm[[arm]]
      ix[sample.int(length(ix), length(ix), replace = TRUE)]
    }), use.names = FALSE)
    w <- tabulate(drawn, nbins = length(participant_ids))
    rep_frame <- base %>%
      mutate(stranger_overlap = stranger_overlap_given(inp, w),
             self_minus_stranger = self_overlap - stranger_overlap)
    rep_frame <- rep_frame[drawn, , drop = FALSE]
    reps[b, ] <- c(selfsim_arm_coef(rep_frame), selfsim_levels(rep_frame))
  }

  coef_draws <- reps[, 1]
  coef_draws <- coef_draws[!is.na(coef_draws)]
  p_boot <- if (length(coef_draws) == 0) NA_real_ else
    min(1, 2 * (min(sum(coef_draws <= 0), sum(coef_draws >= 0)) + 1) /
          (length(coef_draws) + 1))

  ci <- function(x) unname(quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE))
  ci_coef <- ci(reps[, 1])
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      quantity = "arm_difference_AI_minus_Human",
      role     = "registered comparison",
      estimate = obs_coef,
      ci_lo    = if (status == "ok") ci_coef[1] else NA_real_,
      ci_hi    = if (status == "ok") ci_coef[2] else NA_real_,
      p_raw    = if (status == "ok") p_boot else NA_real_,
      n_valid  = length(coef_draws),
      model    = "self_minus_stranger ~ Type + mean_words, ordinary least squares",
      predicted_direction = "AI > Human"
    ),
    tibble(
      quantity = names(obs_levels),
      role     = "description, raw level by arm",
      estimate = unname(obs_levels),
      ci_lo    = apply(reps[, -1, drop = FALSE], 2, function(x) ci(x)[1]),
      ci_hi    = apply(reps[, -1, drop = FALSE], 2, function(x) ci(x)[2]),
      p_raw    = NA_real_,
      n_valid  = apply(reps[, -1, drop = FALSE], 2, function(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
      model    = "mean",
      predicted_direction = NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      dimension      = dim_name,
      B              = B_BOOT,
      seed           = SELFSIM_SEED,
      resampled      = paste0("participants within arm, with replacement; ",
                              "stranger baseline rebuilt from the drawn ",
                              "participants in each replicate"),
      n_participants = sum(!is.na(base$self_minus_stranger)),
      n_human        = sum(!is.na(base$self_minus_stranger) & base$Type == "Human"),
      n_ai           = sum(!is.na(base$self_minus_stranger) & base$Type == "AI"),
      status         = status,
      note           = note
    )
}

selfsim_by_arm <- run_or_report(
  "8.2 within-person word overlap by arm, both dimensions, Holm across the two",
  function() {
    out <- bind_rows(lapply(DIM_LEVELS, selfsim_dimension))
    is_test <- out$role == "registered comparison"
    out$p_holm <- NA_real_
    out$p_holm[is_test] <- p.adjust(out$p_raw[is_test], method = "holm",
                                    n = sum(is_test))
    out %>%
      mutate(reading = case_when(
        role != "registered comparison" ~ NA_character_,
        !status %in% ELIGIBLE_STATUS | is.na(p_holm) ~ NA_character_,
        p_holm < 0.05 & estimate > 0 ~ "supported",
        p_holm < 0.05 & estimate < 0 ~ "opposite direction",
        TRUE ~ "inconclusive"
      )) %>%
      relocate(dimension, role, quantity, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_raw,
               p_holm, reading)
  }
)

if (!is.null(selfsim_by_arm)) {
  selfsim_by_arm %>%
    select(dimension, role, quantity, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_raw, p_holm,
           n_valid, reading) %>%
    print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
  write_csv(selfsim_by_arm,
            file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"))

  # The reading, in words, one block per dimension.
  for (dim_name in DIM_LEVELS) {
    s    <- selfsim_by_arm %>% filter(dimension == dim_name)
    diff <- s %>% filter(role == "registered comparison")
    lvl  <- function(q) s$estimate[s$quantity == q]

    cat("\nWithin-person word overlap, ", dim_name, " explanations (",
        diff$n_human, " human-arm and ", diff$n_ai, " AI-arm participants):\n",
        "  Raw self overlap: Human ", fmt_num(lvl("self_overlap_Human")),
        ", AI ", fmt_num(lvl("self_overlap_AI")),
        "; stranger baseline: Human ", fmt_num(lvl("stranger_overlap_Human")),
        ", AI ", fmt_num(lvl("stranger_overlap_AI")),
        "; content words per explanation: Human ",
        fmt_num(lvl("mean_words_Human"), 1), ", AI ",
        fmt_num(lvl("mean_words_AI"), 1), ".\n",
        "  Own-word reuse beyond strangers (self minus stranger): Human ",
        fmt_num(lvl("self_minus_stranger_Human")), ", AI ",
        fmt_num(lvl("self_minus_stranger_AI")), ".\n",
        "  Arm difference at equal length, AI minus Human: ",
        fmt_num(diff$estimate), " (95% interval ", fmt_num(diff$ci_lo),
        " to ", fmt_num(diff$ci_hi), "; ", diff$n_valid, " of ", diff$B,
        " replicates defined); p ", fmt_num(diff$p_raw, 4), ", Holm-adjusted ",
        fmt_num(diff$p_holm, 4), ". Predicted: AI > Human.\n",
        "  Reading: ", ifelse(is.na(diff$reading),
                              paste0("none, status ", diff$status),
                              diff$reading), ".\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\nThis is the text version of the fourth registered prediction about ",
      "the ratings and is reported wherever it falls; the verdict on that ",
      "prediction itself is read in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.8. An ",
      "inconclusive reading is not evidence that the arms reuse their words ",
      "equally.\n", sep = "")
}

# WHAT TO LOOK AT: the sign of the arm difference, its Holm-adjusted p and
# the reading, then the raw levels beneath it. A difference that appears in
# the raw self_overlap but not in the adjusted difference was a difference in
# how much people wrote.
```

---

# 9. General text description, run in every study

Sections 3 to 8 put fixed questions to the words. This section describes them
more broadly, in the same form in every study where a rating exists, as
exploratory description with no predictions and no verdicts. It describes
three things. The first is the tone and concreteness of the words people
chose, scored against published word norms (9.1). The second is what the
explanations talk about, as found by a topic model that was given no word
list in advance (9.2). The third is which words a predictive model leans on
when it guesses the arm or the rating from the words (9.3).

Every input here comes from the notebook's blind measurement step: the norm
scores, the topic weights and the word counts were all computed without the
arm or the rating, and this file is where the arm and the rating are joined
back. The p-values in 9.1 and 9.2 are corrected by the Benjamini-Hochberg
procedure within each block. The procedure holds the expected share of false
positives among the results called positive, so that a reader scanning a
long table is not misled by the number of rows. The correction makes the
rows easier to read; it does not make them confirmatory.

One limit governs all three, and it is the one section 4.4 sets out. Every
explanation was written after the rating it explains. A difference in tone
between the arms, a topic that goes with higher ratings, or a word a model
leans on to pick out the arm describes what people wrote once their number
was chosen. None of it is a mechanism, and none of it says what produced the
rating.

## 9.1 Tone and concreteness of the words

```{r general-affect}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE MEASURES. nlp/study1_text_affect.csv gives each response four scores,
# each the mean, over the response's content words that have an entry in a
# published norm, of that norm:
#
#   valence      how pleasant a word is, 1 (unhappy) to 9 (happy)
#   arousal      how calm or excited it makes a reader, 1 to 9
#   dominance    how much in control it makes a reader feel, 1 to 9
#                (all three from Warriner, Kuperman and Brysbaert, 2013)
#   concreteness how much a word refers to something that can be seen or
#                touched, 1 (abstract) to 5 (concrete) (Brysbaert, Warriner
#                and Kuperman, 2014)
#
# Before scoring, the notebook removes the rating questions' own words, so
# that "creative" and "effort" do not drive every score, and a word with no
# exact entry is tried once more with a final s, es, ed or ing removed. A
# response with no word in a norm has no score on it and drops out of that
# model; n_vad_matched and n_conc_matched say how many words matched.
#
# THE MODEL, per dimension and per measure:
#
#   score ~ Type * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)
#
# where rating_c is the rating minus that dimension's mean rating over all
# responses. Centring makes the TypeAI coefficient the arm difference in the
# score (AI minus Human) at the average rating, rather than at a rating of
# zero, which the scale does not have. The TypeAI:rating_c coefficient is the
# arm by rating interaction: how much more (or less) the score climbs with
# each rating point in the AI arm than in the human arm. Holding the rating in
# the model matters because the arms gave different ratings and a higher
# rating goes with warmer words; without it, an arm difference in valence
# would mostly be the rating difference again. The random intercepts give
# each participant and each image their own baseline, as everywhere in this
# file.
#
# The two coefficients from each of the eight models (two dimensions by four
# measures) are corrected together, sixteen p-values, by Benjamini-Hochberg.
# Raw means by arm sit beside them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))

affect <- read_csv(
  PATH_AFFECT,
  col_types = cols(
    id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
    dimension = col_character(), n_content_words = col_integer(),
    n_vad_matched = col_integer(), valence = col_double(),
    arousal = col_double(), dominance = col_double(),
    n_conc_matched = col_integer(), concreteness = col_double()
  )
)
check_blind_columns(affect, AFFECT_COLS, "The affect file")
check_response_keys(affect, "The affect file")

AFFECT_MEASURES <- c("valence", "arousal", "dominance", "concreteness")

# The rating centred within each dimension, used by 9.1 and 9.2 alike.
rating_centres <- ratings %>%
  group_by(dimension) %>%
  summarise(rating_centre = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

affect_joined <- affect %>%
  mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = DIM_LEVELS)) %>%
  inner_join(ratings, by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension")) %>%
  left_join(rating_centres, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(rating_c = rating - rating_centre,
         Type     = factor(Type, levels = TYPE_LEVELS))
stopifnot(nrow(affect_joined) == nrow(affect))

AFFECT_TERMS <- c(
  "TypeAI"          = "arm difference (AI minus Human) at the average rating",
  "TypeAI:rating_c" = "arm by rating interaction (AI minus Human, per rating point)"
)

affect_by_arm <- run_or_report(
  "9.1 tone and concreteness by arm, both dimensions, four measures",
  function() {
    rows <- list()
    for (dim_name in DIM_LEVELS) {
      for (m in AFFECT_MEASURES) {
        d <- affect_joined %>%
          filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(.data[[m]])) %>%
          mutate(score = .data[[m]])
        res <- fit_mixed(
          score ~ Type * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), d,
          step = paste0("9.1 ", m, " ~ arm x rating, ", dim_name)
        )
        tm <- tidy_mixed(res) %>%
          filter(is.na(term) | term %in% names(AFFECT_TERMS))
        if (all(is.na(tm$term))) {
          tm <- tibble(term = names(AFFECT_TERMS), estimate = NA_real_,
                       std.error = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
                       statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_,
                       conf.low = NA_real_, conf.high = NA_real_,
                       status = res$status, note = res$note)
        }
        rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- tm %>%
          transmute(
            dimension = dim_name, measure = m, term,
            quantity  = unname(AFFECT_TERMS[term]),
            estimate, std_error = std.error, df, t = statistic,
            p_raw = p.value, ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
            mean_Human = mean(d$score[d$Type == "Human"]),
            mean_AI    = mean(d$score[d$Type == "AI"]),
            n_scored   = nrow(d),
            n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
            rating_centre  = d$rating_centre[1],
            status, note,
            model = paste0(m, " ~ Type * rating_c + (1 | id) + ",
                           "(1 | stimulus_id), REML, bobyqa; rating_c is the ",
                           "rating minus the dimension's mean rating")
          )
      }
    }
    out <- bind_rows(rows)
    out %>%
      mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH", n = nrow(out)),
             .after = p_raw)
  }
)

if (!is.null(affect_by_arm)) {
  affect_by_arm %>%
    select(dimension, measure, term, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_raw, p_bh,
           mean_Human, mean_AI, n_scored, status) %>%
    print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
  write_csv(affect_by_arm,
            file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))
}

# WHAT TO LOOK AT: the TypeAI rows, which say whether the arms chose warmer,
# more excited, more in-control or more concrete words at the same rating,
# and the interaction rows, which say whether the words warm with the rating
# at the same pace in both arms. Description of the vocabulary only.
```

## 9.2 What the explanations talk about

```{r general-topics}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE TOPICS. nlp/study1_text_topics.csv gives each response a weight on each
# topic of a topic model fitted by the notebook: non-negative matrix
# factorisation, which writes the table of responses by words as the product
# of two tables with no negative entries, one giving each response's weight
# on each topic and the other each topic's weight on each word. It is fitted
# separately to the creativity and the effort explanations, on content words
# weighted by tf-idf (a word's count scaled down by how many responses use
# it), with the function words and the rating questions' own words removed,
# and without the arm or the rating. The number of topics in each dimension
# was chosen by the stability rule written into the notebook, and each
# response's weights sum to one, so a weight is the share of that response
# the topic accounts for. A response with no kept word has no weights and
# drops out here. tables/text_topics_top_words.csv lists each topic's ten
# heaviest words, and the five heaviest label the topic below.
#
# THE MODEL, per dimension and per topic:
#
#   weight ~ Type + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)
#
# with rating_c centred as in 9.1. The TypeAI coefficient is the arm
# difference in the topic's weight at the same rating; the rating term is
# kept beside it so that a topic that simply goes with high or low ratings is
# not credited to the arm.
#
# THE TEST OF THE ARM TERM. Topic weights are bounded between zero and one
# and pile up at zero, so the arm term's usual standard error leans on
# assumptions these data do not meet well. The arm term is therefore tested
# against a permutation null instead: the arm labels are dealt out afresh
# among the participants (each participant keeping one label, as in 8.1),
# the model is refitted, and the arm term's t value (its estimate over its
# standard error) is recorded, 200 times. The p-value is the share of
# shuffles, counting the observed data as one, whose t value is at least as
# far from zero as the observed one. The same 200 shuffles serve every topic
# in a dimension, they are drawn before the parallel section from a fixed
# seed, and the p-values are corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg within each
# dimension. Mean weights by arm sit beside each row.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))

N_TOPIC_PERM    <- 200L
TOPIC_PERM_SEED <- 20260421L

topics <- read_csv(
  PATH_TOPICS,
  col_types = cols(id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
                   dimension = col_character(), topic = col_integer(),
                   weight = col_double())
)
check_blind_columns(topics, TOPICS_COLS, "The topic file")

topic_words <- read_csv(
  PATH_TOPIC_WORDS,
  col_types = cols(dimension = col_character(), topic = col_integer(),
                   rank = col_integer(), word = col_character(),
                   weight = col_double())
)
check_blind_columns(topic_words, TOPIC_WORDS_COLS, "The topic word list")

# Every response appears once with every topic of its dimension.
topic_keys <- topics %>% distinct(id, stimulus_id, dimension)
check_response_keys(topic_keys, "The topic file")
topic_grid <- topics %>% count(dimension, id, stimulus_id, name = "n_topics") %>%
  left_join(topics %>% group_by(dimension) %>%
              summarise(k = n_distinct(topic), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "dimension")
if (any(topic_grid$n_topics != topic_grid$k)) {
  stop("The topic file does not give every response one weight per topic.")
}

topic_labels <- topic_words %>%
  filter(rank <= 5) %>%
  arrange(dimension, topic, rank) %>%
  group_by(dimension, topic) %>%
  summarise(topic_label = paste(word, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")

topics_joined <- topics %>%
  filter(!is.na(weight)) %>%
  mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = DIM_LEVELS)) %>%
  inner_join(ratings, by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension")) %>%
  left_join(rating_centres, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(rating_c = rating - rating_centre,
         Type     = factor(Type, levels = TYPE_LEVELS))

# The arm term's t value from one refit, for the permutation null. lme4 is
# called directly here, without lmerTest's degrees of freedom, because only
# the t value is needed; a refit that fails gives NA and is counted.
topic_t <- function(d) {
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    lme4::lmer(weight ~ Type + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
               data = d, REML = TRUE,
               control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  )), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NA_real_)
  co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  if (!"TypeAI" %in% rownames(co)) return(NA_real_)
  unname(co["TypeAI", "t value"])
}

topics_dimension <- function(dim_name) {
  d_dim  <- topics_joined %>% filter(dimension == dim_name)
  k_set  <- sort(unique(d_dim$topic))
  id_arm <- d_dim %>% distinct(id, Type) %>% arrange(id)

  set.seed(TOPIC_PERM_SEED)
  shuffles <- replicate(N_TOPIC_PERM, {
    setNames(sample(as.character(id_arm$Type)), id_arm$id)
  }, simplify = FALSE)

  bind_rows(lapply(k_set, function(k) {
    d <- d_dim %>% filter(topic == k)
    res <- fit_mixed(weight ~ Type + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
                     d, step = paste0("9.2 topic ", k, " weight ~ arm + rating, ",
                                      dim_name))
    eligible <- res$status %in% ELIGIBLE_STATUS
    co <- if (is.null(res$fit)) NULL else summary(res$fit)$coefficients
    t_obs <- if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["TypeAI", "t value"])
    t_null <- run_permutations(shuffles, function(lab) {
      dd <- d
      dd$Type <- factor(lab[dd$id], levels = TYPE_LEVELS)
      topic_t(dd)
    })
    n_valid <- sum(!is.na(t_null))
    p_perm  <- if (!eligible || is.na(t_obs) || n_valid == 0) NA_real_ else
      (1 + sum(abs(t_null) >= abs(t_obs), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + n_valid)
    tibble(
      dimension  = dim_name,
      topic      = k,
      quantity   = "arm difference in topic weight (AI minus Human) at the same rating",
      estimate   = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["TypeAI", "Estimate"]),
      std_error  = if (eligible) unname(co["TypeAI", "Std. Error"]) else NA_real_,
      t          = if (eligible) t_obs else NA_real_,
      p_perm     = p_perm,
      n_perm     = N_TOPIC_PERM,
      n_perm_valid = n_valid,
      perm_seed  = TOPIC_PERM_SEED,
      rating_estimate = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["rating_c", "Estimate"]),
      mean_weight_Human = mean(d$weight[d$Type == "Human"]),
      mean_weight_AI    = mean(d$weight[d$Type == "AI"]),
      n_responses    = nrow(d),
      n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
      status = res$status,
      note   = res$note,
      model  = paste0("weight ~ Type + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), ",
                      "REML, bobyqa; arm term tested against arm labels ",
                      "shuffled across participants")
    )
  })) %>%
    mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH", n = n()), .after = p_perm)
}

topics_by_arm <- run_or_report(
  "9.2 topic weights by arm, permutation test of the arm term, both dimensions",
  function() {
    bind_rows(lapply(DIM_LEVELS, topics_dimension)) %>%
      left_join(topic_labels, by = c("dimension", "topic")) %>%
      relocate(topic_label, .after = topic)
  }
)

if (!is.null(topics_by_arm)) {
  topics_by_arm %>%
    select(dimension, topic, topic_label, mean_weight_Human, mean_weight_AI,
           estimate, p_perm, p_bh, status) %>%
    print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
  write_csv(topics_by_arm,
            file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))
}

# WHAT TO LOOK AT: the topics whose mean weight differs most between the arms
# at the same rating, read through their labels. A topic carried more by one
# arm says what that arm wrote about more, after the number was chosen.
```

## 9.3 Which words a prediction leans on

```{r general-prediction-weights}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE QUESTION. Section 8.1 asks how well the words predict, with ridge
# models that spread small weights across every word. This asks which words
# do the predicting, with the lasso, a penalised regression whose penalty sets
# most coefficients to exactly zero, so that only the words a prediction
# cannot do without keep a weight. Two models per dimension:
#
#   arm    a lasso logistic regression of the arm on the word counts, with
#          the rating in the model and left unpenalised (penalty factor 0),
#          so a word keeps a weight only if it helps tell the arms apart
#          beyond what the rating does;
#   rating a lasso linear regression of the rating on the word counts.
#
# HOW STRONG THE PENALTY IS. The penalty is chosen by ten-fold
# cross-validation grouped by participant, with the same outer folds as 8.1,
# and with the vocabulary built inside each training fold by the same
# five-response floor. glmnet's own cross-validation routine cannot rebuild
# the vocabulary fold by fold, so the folds are run here directly: for each
# fold the training responses set the vocabulary, the lasso path is fitted on
# them over a common grid of penalties, and the held-out responses are scored
# (binomial deviance for the arm, squared error for the rating). The chosen
# penalty is lambda.1se, the strongest penalty whose cross-validated error is
# within one standard error of the best, glmnet's usual choice when the aim
# is a short and stable list of words. The model is then refitted on every
# response, with the vocabulary built from every response, at that penalty,
# and the words with a nonzero coefficient are reported with their signs.
#
# HOW TO READ A WEIGHT. A coefficient is the change in the log-odds of the AI
# arm (arm model) or in the rating (rating model) for one more use of the
# word in an explanation, after the lasso's shrinkage. A positive weight in
# the arm model is a word that goes with the machine arm at the same rating;
# a positive weight in the rating model is a word that goes with a higher
# rating. Among words that move together the lasso tends to keep one and drop
# the rest, so a word missing from the list may still go with the outcome,
# and a kept word stands for its group. None of this tests a word.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_prediction_weights.csv"))

# Held-out loss for a matrix of predictions (one column per penalty), on the
# response scale: binomial deviance with the probabilities kept a little away
# from zero and one, as glmnet does, or squared error.
heldout_loss <- function(pred, y, family) {
  if (family == "binomial") {
    p <- pmin(pmax(pred, 1e-5), 1 - 1e-5)
    -2 * (y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p))
  } else {
    (y - pred)^2
  }
}

lasso_weights_for <- function(dim_name, target) {
  fr     <- dimension_frame(dim_name)
  resp   <- fr$resp
  counts <- fr$counts
  family <- if (target == "arm") "binomial" else "gaussian"
  y      <- if (target == "arm") as.integer(resp$Type == "AI") else resp$rating

  set.seed(RECOVER_SEED)
  outer_by_id <- participant_folds(fr$id_arm, N_OUTER_FOLDS)
  outer_fold  <- unname(outer_by_id[resp$id])

  build_x <- function(words) {
    X <- response_word_matrix(resp, counts, words)
    if (target == "arm") {
      X <- cbind(Matrix::Matrix(resp$rating, ncol = 1, sparse = TRUE,
                                dimnames = list(NULL, "rating")), X)
    }
    X
  }
  pen <- function(X) if (target == "arm") c(0, rep(1, ncol(X) - 1)) else
    rep(1, ncol(X))

  # The full-data vocabulary and fit, which also set the common penalty grid.
  vocab_all <- floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, rep(TRUE, nrow(resp)))
  X_all     <- build_x(vocab_all$word)
  fitted    <- with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(X_all, y, family = family,
                                            alpha = 1,
                                            penalty.factor = pen(X_all)))
  full_fit  <- fitted$value
  lam       <- full_fit$lambda
  warns     <- fitted$warnings

  fold_loss <- matrix(NA_real_, N_OUTER_FOLDS, length(lam))
  fold_n    <- integer(N_OUTER_FOLDS)
  for (k in seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {
    tr <- outer_fold != k
    Xk <- build_x(floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, tr)$word)
    fk <- with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(Xk[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr],
                                       family = family, alpha = 1,
                                       lambda = lam,
                                       penalty.factor = pen(Xk)))
    warns <- c(warns, fk$warnings)
    pk <- predict(fk$value, Xk[!tr, , drop = FALSE], s = lam,
                  type = "response")
    fold_loss[k, ] <- colMeans(heldout_loss(as.matrix(pk), y[!tr], family))
    fold_n[k]      <- sum(!tr)
  }
  cvm  <- apply(fold_loss, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n)
  cvsd <- sqrt(apply(sweep(fold_loss, 2, cvm)^2, 2, weighted.mean,
                     w = fold_n) / (N_OUTER_FOLDS - 1))
  i_min      <- which.min(cvm)
  lambda_min <- lam[i_min]
  lambda_1se <- max(lam[cvm <= cvm[i_min] + cvsd[i_min]])

  warns  <- unique(warns)
  status <- if (length(warns) == 0) "ok" else "nonconvergence"
  note   <- if (length(warns) == 0) "status ok; no warning from any fit" else
    paste0("status nonconvergence; ", paste(warns, collapse = "; "))

  b <- as.matrix(coef(full_fit, s = lambda_1se))[, 1]
  rating_coef <- if (target == "arm") unname(b["rating"]) else NA_real_
  b <- b[setdiff(names(b), c("(Intercept)", "rating"))]
  b <- b[b != 0]

  # The labels are settled here, outside the table, because inside mutate()
  # the name `target` would refer to the table's column of that name.
  is_arm      <- target == "arm"
  loss_text   <- if (family == "binomial") "binomial deviance" else
    "squared error"
  model_text  <- if (is_arm) {
    paste0("lasso logistic regression (glmnet, alpha = 1), arm on the ",
           "rating (penalty factor 0) and the word counts; penalty at ",
           "lambda.1se from ten-fold cross-validation grouped by ",
           "participant with the vocabulary rebuilt in each training ",
           "fold; refitted on all responses")
  } else {
    paste0("lasso linear regression (glmnet, alpha = 1), rating on the ",
           "word counts; penalty at lambda.1se from ten-fold ",
           "cross-validation grouped by participant with the vocabulary ",
           "rebuilt in each training fold; refitted on all responses")
  }

  base <- tibble(
    dimension  = dim_name,
    target     = target,
    predictors = if (is_arm) "words, with the rating unpenalised" else "words"
  )
  words_tbl <- if (length(b) == 0) {
    base %>% mutate(word = NA_character_, coefficient = NA_real_,
                    sign = NA_character_, rank = NA_integer_,
                    n_responses_word = NA_integer_)
  } else {
    tibble(word = names(b), coefficient = unname(b)) %>%
      mutate(dimension  = base$dimension, target = base$target,
             predictors = base$predictors, .before = 1) %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(coefficient > 0, "positive", "negative"),
             rank = as.integer(rank(-abs(coefficient),
                                    ties.method = "first"))) %>%
      left_join(vocab_all %>% rename(n_responses_word = n_responses),
                by = "word") %>%
      arrange(rank)
  }
  words_tbl %>%
    mutate(
      rating_coefficient = rating_coef,
      lambda_1se   = lambda_1se,
      lambda_min   = lambda_min,
      n_words_in_model = nrow(vocab_all),
      n_nonzero    = length(b),
      cv_loss      = loss_text,
      n_folds      = N_OUTER_FOLDS,
      seed         = RECOVER_SEED,
      n_responses  = nrow(resp),
      status       = status,
      note         = note,
      model        = model_text
    )
}

prediction_weights <- run_or_report(
  "9.3 lasso weights on words for the arm and the rating, both dimensions",
  function() {
    bind_rows(lapply(DIM_LEVELS, function(dim_name) {
      bind_rows(lasso_weights_for(dim_name, "arm"),
                lasso_weights_for(dim_name, "rating"))
    }))
  }
)

if (!is.null(prediction_weights)) {
  write_csv(prediction_weights,
            file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_text_prediction_weights.csv"))
  for (dim_name in DIM_LEVELS) {
    for (tg in c("arm", "rating")) {
      pw <- prediction_weights %>%
        filter(dimension == dim_name, target == tg)
      cat("\n", dim_name, " explanations, ", tg, " model (", pw$status[1],
          "): ", pw$n_nonzero[1], " of ", pw$n_words_in_model[1],
          " words keep a weight at lambda.1se",
          if (tg == "arm") paste0("; the unpenalised rating coefficient is ",
                                  fmt_num(pw$rating_coefficient[1])) else "",
          ".\n", sep = "")
      if (pw$n_nonzero[1] > 0) {
        top <- pw %>% filter(rank <= 10)
        cat("  ", paste(sprintf("%s (%+.3f)", top$word, top$coefficient),
                        collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
      }
    }
  }
}

# WHAT TO LOOK AT: the positive and negative words of the arm model, which
# are the words the two arms used differently at the same rating, and the
# words of the rating model, which are the words that went with higher and
# lower ratings. Both describe what was written after the rating.
```

## 10.1 Percentages by category, with intervals

```{r fig-text-prevalence, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.5}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two panels in the same greyscale style as Study1_01_Quant.Rmd.
#
# Panel A: what effort talk was about in the human-attribution arm, the
#   answer to question 1 in one picture.
# Panel B: how often each arm mentioned prompting in an effort justification,
#   the scale against which the leak count in section 5 is read.
#
# Error bars are the participant-resampled 95% intervals computed above. They
# are the same numbers as the CSVs; nothing is recomputed for the figure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, c("study1_fig3_text_prevalence.pdf",
                                        "study1_fig3_text_prevalence.png")),
              file.path(PATH_PAPER_FIG, "study1_fig3_text_prevalence.pdf"))

fig_prevalence <- run_or_report("10.1 prevalence figure", function() {

  stopifnot(!is.null(effort_prevalence), !is.null(prompt_by_arm))

  panel_a_dat <- effort_prevalence %>%
    filter(quantity != "none_of_the_three") %>%
    mutate(
      label = recode(quantity,
                     detail = "Detail talk",
                     time   = "Time talk",
                     skill  = "Skill talk"),
      label = factor(label, levels = c("Detail talk", "Time talk",
                                       "Skill talk"))
    )

  panel_a <- ggplot(panel_a_dat, aes(x = label, y = estimate)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.62, fill = FILL_NEUTRAL) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi),
                  width = 0.14, linewidth = 0.4, color = "black") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
    labs(
      x        = NULL,
      y        = "Share of effort justifications",
      title    = "A  What effort talk was about",
      subtitle = "Human-attribution arm; 95% intervals from resampling participants"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "grey30"),
      axis.text     = element_text(color = "black")
    )

  panel_b_dat <- prompt_by_arm %>%
    mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = TYPE_LEVELS))

  panel_b <- ggplot(panel_b_dat, aes(x = arm, y = estimate, fill = arm)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi),
                  width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.4, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PALETTE_TYPE) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
    labs(
      x        = "Attributed creator",
      y        = "Share mentioning prompting",
      title    = "B  Machine talk in effort justifications",
      subtitle = "Any mention in the Human arm is a leak from the cover story"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "grey30"),
      axis.text       = element_text(color = "black")
    )

  panel_a + panel_b + plot_layout(widths = c(1.25, 1))
})

if (!is.null(fig_prevalence)) {
  print(fig_prevalence)
  ggsave(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_fig3_text_prevalence.pdf"),
         fig_prevalence, width = 7.5, height = 4.2, device = cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_fig3_text_prevalence.png"),
         fig_prevalence, width = 7.5, height = 4.2, dpi = 300)

}
```
